conventions.convention: The period-L torus carries normalized measure L^(-d) dx; frequencies are κ_k = 2πk/L, Sobolev weights are (1 + L²|κ_k|²)^s, and the constant velocity mode is unrestricted, with P_0 = I.

On a nonempty bounded open subset of R³, H is the L² closure of compactly supported smooth divergence-free fields and V is their H_0¹ closure. Spatial measure is unnormalized. No identification with all divergence-free H_0¹ fields or pointwise boundary trace is asserted.

C_w consists of actual maps with continuous fixed Hilbert-space pairings; Bochner spaces consist of almost-everywhere classes of strongly measurable maps. A weakly continuous representative, when it exists, is unique. Local time membership means membership on every interval (0,T).

Leray–Hopf velocities strongly attain their initial data, obey the initial energy inequality at every time, and obey restart inequalities for every later time from each starting time in one full-measure set, together with zero.

Periodic distributions are continuous complex-linear functionals with bilinear pairings; derivatives transpose test derivatives with a minus sign. Matrix divergence is row-wise: (div A)_i = Σ_j ∂_j A_ij.

Periodic pressure is normalized by vanishing zero spatial Fourier coefficient; rectangular pressure is normalized by annihilating a(t)θ(x), where θ is one fixed compactly supported spatial test of integral one.

Rectangular pressure recovery assumes a linear divergence right inverse with compact output-support enlargement and fixed-support derivative-seminorm continuity; its real-linear supplier is explicitly complexified in the proof.

load_bearing.statement: Defines the normalized period-L Fourier spaces H, V and H^(-r), unrestricted zero mode, solenoidal projection P and rectangular truncations; the analytic coefficient-space and divergence identifications assume Countable Choice.
For nonempty bounded open Ω ⊂ R³, H is the L² closure of D_σ(Ω), and V is its closure in H_0¹, with squared V norm equal to the sum of squared L² field and gradient norms.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. For every nonempty bounded open Ω ⊂ R³, H and V are separable Hilbert spaces, V embeds continuously and densely in H, and there is a countable H-orthonormal sequence in D_σ(Ω) whose finite span is dense in both H and V.

Under Countable Choice, continuous finite-Fourier-sum curves with uniform H bounds, integrated gradient bounds and fixed-mode Lipschitz constants have a subsequence converging uniformly in every Fourier coefficient, strongly in L²(0,T;H), and, after further extraction, strongly in H almost everywhere, to a weakly continuous energy-space limit with the stated bounds.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. For the stated bounded closure spaces and smooth solenoidal basis, V embeds compactly in H, and there are δ_K decreasing to zero such that ||(I − Π_K)a||_H ≤ δ_K ||a||_V for every a ∈ V.

Under the Axiom of Choice, zero-boundary fields in three dimensions satisfy the domain-independent L⁶ gradient estimate and L⁴ interpolation estimate. Energy-space velocities belong to L^(8/3)(0,T;L⁴), and their quadratic transport defines a strongly measurable, representative-independent class in L^(4/3)(0,T;V*).

Assume Countable Choice. Let d ≥ 2, L > 0, ν > 0, and u_0 ∈ H for the periodic solenoidal Fourier spaces. Then there exists a global unforced periodic Leray–Hopf solution with data (ν,u_0). No uniqueness or global smoothness is asserted.

For bounded open Ω ⊂ R³, the stated bounded closure spaces, the Axiom of Choice, ν > 0 and u_0 ∈ H, there exists a global weakly continuous energy-space velocity with strong initial trace, the variational identity for compactly supported C¹ V-valued tests, and initial and full-measure restart energy inequalities.

Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice. A global periodic Leray–Hopf velocity and a given smooth divergence-free velocity with smooth pressure, the same viscosity and initial data agree in H at every time of the smooth interval.

concerns.concern: Proof 1.1 says to extract subsequences successively over the countable coefficient/rational-time pairs and 'use Countable Choice for the resulting nested subsequences'. Arbitrary successive choices depend on earlier choices, so that sentence alone does not justify the construction using Countable Choice. A deterministic extraction rule closes the gap: order the finitely many subcubes, retain the first admissible one, and select least admissible increasing indices. The theorem need not acquire a Dependent Choice hypothesis.

The witness u_n(x) = sin(2πn x_1/L)e_2 does not specify its starting index, while step 2.1 claims the constant-test integral is 1/2 'for every n'. At n = 0 the integral is zero. Specify n ≥ 1, or qualify that equality accordingly; the counterexample and limiting argument remain valid.

seams_checked.note: The actual item dependency is rectangular evolving pressure's use of the rectangular test-divergence inverse. Both interfaces retain finite rectangles, zero-integral inputs, compact support enlargement and fixed-support derivative-seminorm continuity. The consumer explicitly complexifies the real supplier. The current supplier now includes finite-integral Fubini and parameter-differentiation justifications in steps 1.2–2.1, supported by four declared published prerequisites; the older open ledger description does not describe these current proof bytes. The two pages' differing periodic Sobolev normalizations are not silently identified by this use.

Opened all six fd-w02 items. Periodic consumers retain normalized measure, unrestricted mean mode, positive viscosity, strong initial trace and the initial/restart energy quantifiers. Smooth consistency carries both choice assumptions and uses uniqueness only on the supplied smooth interval. Bounded consumers retain closure-defined no-slip spaces and AC; rectangular pressure retains its explicit divergence-inverse hypothesis and distribution-only conclusion. Physical energy scaling restores unnormalized volume integrals. These are conditional model deductions without empirical universality claims.
